title: runtime: add CLI flags to force kernel choice + dump kernel-selection trace
author: Omar El-Sayed
description:
Adds runtime CLI/debug flags to (a) force a specific kernel implementation for a given run and (b) dump a structured kernel-selection trace to disk/stdout. This is primarily for triage/customer escalations where we need to reproduce tail latency issues and confirm whether a mis-selection occurred without relying on sampled telemetry. The dump intentionally excludes prompts/tokens and is safe to attach to support tickets.

Motivation: During 1.21 canary we had a few long-context regressions that were hard to root-cause quickly because selection telemetry is sampled and the oncall path often starts from a single request trace. This PR makes it possible to: (1) pin a kernel to validate “selection vs kernel perf” hypotheses, (2) capture the selector’s feature vector + candidate list + decision path for offline review, and (3) do this in Dedicated/Private environments where we can’t depend on Redwood-hosted dashboards.

New flags:
- --kernel.force=<kernel_id>: bypass selector and force the requested kernel (still validates kernel exists + is compatible with model arch; otherwise hard-fails fast).
- --kernel.selection.dump[=path]: enable dumping of selection decisions; if path is omitted, writes to stderr.
- --kernel.selection.dump-format=(json|text) (default json)
- --kernel.selection.dump-sampling=<0.0-1.0> (default 1.0 when explicitly enabled)
- --kernel.selection.dump-max-bytes=<n> (default 1048576) to avoid runaway logs.
- --kernel.selection.dump-include-candidates=(true|false) (default true) (can be disabled to reduce size/cardinality).

Dump contents (json): selector_version, request_id (runtime-internal UUID), model_id, model_family, gpu_sku (normalized), driver/cuda versions, seq_len_prefill, seq_len_decode_target, seq_bucket, workload_hints (if present), gate_state (v1/v2), chosen_kernel, fallback_chain (if any), candidate_kernels (optional), and decision_reasons (ordered list).

Safety/behavior notes:
- Prompt content/tokens are never included.
- When --kernel.force is set, the dump explicitly records that selection was bypassed.
- Dumping is best-effort: failures to write the dump never fail the request path unless --kernel.selection.dump-required=true is set (not added here; left as follow-up if needed).
- Overhead: selector dump is behind an explicit flag; sampling and max-bytes cap are intended to keep impact bounded when enabled in prod.

Examples:
- Force a kernel for a local repro:
  runtime serve --model llama-3.1-70b --kernel.force=flashattn_v3_h100
- Capture decision trace for a single run (stderr):
  runtime bench --scenario long_context --kernel.selection.dump --kernel.selection.dump-format=json
- Capture trace to file with sampling:
  runtime serve --kernel.selection.dump=/tmp/ksel.ndjson --kernel.selection.dump-sampling=0.05

Testing:
- Added unit tests for flag parsing and forced-kernel compatibility checks.
- Added an integration test that validates deterministic dump fields (no timestamps; stable key ordering for text mode).
- Verified no new metrics/telemetry are emitted by default.

Follow-ups:
- Update runbook to reference these flags (separate doc PR).
- Consider plumbing a config-file equivalent for Private deployments that don’t use CLI flags directly.
commits: runtime/cli: plumb kernel selection debug options into server + bench entrypoints
runtime/kernels: implement forced-kernel override with compatibility validation
runtime/kernels: add selection trace dumper (json + text) with sampling and size caps
tests: add unit + integration coverage for flags and dump output stability
docs: add --help entries + examples for oncall triage
review_conversation: Yuki Sato: The force flag should hard-fail if the requested kernel is incompatible with the model family (e.g., trying to force an MLA kernel on a non-MLA arch). Also can we ensure the dump includes selector_version + rule path so we can diff v1/v2 easily?

Omar El-Sayed: Added compatibility validation (family + attention backend requirements) and included selector_version + decision_reasons (ordered) + gate_state. Force path records forced_kernel=true and bypass_reason=cli_force.

Noah Patel: Please ensure determinism/replay: the dump shouldn’t contain wall-clock timestamps or anything derived from address ordering. Also, we should cap file size to avoid someone enabling this on a hot path and filling disks.
Omar El-Sayed: Removed timestamps, stabilized text output key ordering, and added --kernel.selection.dump-max-bytes with a default 1MiB cap; write stops after cap with a truncation marker.

Allison Grant: If this gets used in prod incident response, writing dumps should never fail requests. Can we make dump failures best-effort and clearly surfaced in logs without causing request errors?

Omar El-Sayed: Implemented best-effort writes: failures log a single WARN per process (rate-limited) and continue request execution. Dump enablement remains explicit via CLI. Not adding a 'required' mode in this PR.
Connor O'Brien: Any impact on 1.21 release notes / operational docs? Also flag naming: prefer --kernel.selection.dump-format rather than --kernel.dump-format to keep namespace clean.
Omar El-Sayed: Renamed flags under --kernel.selection.*. Added --help text and a short section in runtime_help.md. Runbook update will be a follow-up PR tied to ENG-4821.

Yuki Sato: Looks good now. One more request: when candidates are included, please redact kernel params that can explode cardinality (e.g., internal tuning knobs). We only need kernel_id + compat tags + score/reason.
Omar El-Sayed: Adjusted candidate serialization to include kernel_id, tags, and (optional) score + rejection reason. Excluded raw tuning knobs/config blobs. Added a regression test for output size.
Allison Grant: Approving; thanks for the size cap + best-effort behavior.
Noah Patel: Approving. Please keep an eye on any accidental exposure of request identifiers; internal UUID is fine as long as it’s not customer PII.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Connor O'Brien
release_notes: Internal: Added runtime CLI flags for oncall/customer triage to force a kernel and dump kernel-selection traces (no prompt content; size-capped; opt-in).
